# FirstTake — full details

Publisher: Sklarstad (https://sklarstad.com/) · Contact: support@sklarstad.com
Product page: https://sklarstad.com/firsttake/
Source code: https://github.com/emersonsklar/firsttake

## Availability

Free and open source under the Apache License 2.0. Download or clone it from
https://github.com/emersonsklar/firsttake. There is nothing to buy; an optional pay-what-you-want page
(https://sklar.gumroad.com/l/support-firsttake) exists for people who want to support it, and unlocks nothing.

## What it is

FirstTake is a skill — a packaged set of instructions and tools an AI coding assistant uses — for
people who shoot and finish video. It is made for Claude Code (terminal, desktop app, web, or VS Code
and JetBrains), and other coding agents can read it and run its tools too. The tools themselves are
plain local programs with no AI model and no network access. It carries a shoot from an empty room to a delivered master,
built around one rule: a principle has to be re-derived on set, a number does not. It runs on the
user's own Mac or Windows computer and never sends footage, or any details about a shoot, to anyone.
(What a user types to their AI assistant is covered by that assistant's own privacy terms.)

Built by working film professionals. Before public release, its tools were in daily use by dozens
of working professionals across documentary, scripted content, interviews and social shorts, with
hundreds of hours of footage put through them. It is actively developed; finishing with no editing software at all is the latest addition.

## Who it's for

Anyone making video who wants professional discipline behind their footage: casual YouTubers and
vloggers, freelance shooters and editors, and studios running full productions.

- Documentary: verified card offload and footage QC for material that can't be reshot.
- Interviews: multi-camera sync with no shared timecode, per-speaker audio, word-level speaker attribution.
- Scripted content: run sheets, call order, and a timeline built from one plan.
- Social shorts and YouTube: vertical cuts with burned-in captions and pull clips from the same master.

## What it does

### Prepare
- Profiles the user's actual kit (not a spec sheet) and measures it.
- Scouts locations from photographs.
- Designs lighting, camera and audio placement as literal numbers.
- Builds checklists, call order and day sheets.

### Capture
- Verified card offload: reads each card once, hashes while reading, then re-reads every destination
  and compares. Writes MHL 1.1, optional generation-chained ASC MHL, a JSON manifest and a
  self-contained HTML report. Detects a single changed byte on a backup.
- Footage QC measured from the files, not the monitor: log-aware exposure, focus stability, frame
  timing and dropped frames, 8-bit video hiding in a 10-bit container, per-channel audio levels,
  cross-camera frame-rate mismatch.
- Card retention rule: cards stay until the deliverable is live and the archive is verified.

### Finish
- Conform: places recordings that share no timecode on one timeline and measures the clock drift a
  clap cannot see (for example 70 frames over 40 minutes).
- Edit: assembles the cut, with transitions and speed ramps. No editing software is required: the
  same plan renders a full-quality master with ffmpeg. Optionally it also builds an editable
  timeline in DaVinci Resolve Studio or Adobe Premiere Pro (early access). Where an application
  can't reproduce something exactly, the build stops and names it rather than approximating.
- Grade: matches cameras, then grades to a reference.
- Mix: per-speaker restoration and levelling, cross-talk ducking driven by word labels, mastering
  to target, and a per-phrase check (a mix can meet every overall target and still have phrases
  4 LU too loud).
- Captions and documents: subtitles with text from speech recognition and timing from a forced
  aligner; a reviewer's transcript and review document.
- Deliver: masters, vertical social cuts with burned-in captions, and pull clips.

## Requirements

- A Mac or Windows computer.
- An AI coding assistant: Claude Code (terminal, desktop app, web, or VS Code / JetBrains), or
  another coding agent.
- Nothing else to install by hand: setup installs everything FirstTake needs, after the user
  agrees, and nothing it doesn't.
- No editing software. DaVinci Resolve Studio or Adobe Premiere Pro (early access) is optional,
  only for an editable timeline.

## Setup

No terminal needed. About ten minutes, mostly downloads.
1. Download FirstTake from https://github.com/emersonsklar/firsttake (Code → Download ZIP) and unzip it,
   or clone it.
2. Open the FirstTake folder in an AI coding assistant (Claude Code in the desktop app, the web, the
   terminal or an editor, or another coding agent).
3. Ask it: "Set up FirstTake for me." It checks the computer and asks before installing anything.
4. A practice run on test footage (a couple of minutes): a verified backup, a deliberately damaged copy
   caught, and a footage check that spots planted problems (silent audio, audio recorded too loud).

## FAQ

- Does footage get uploaded? No. FirstTake runs locally and never sends footage or shoot details to
  anyone.
- Is editing software required? No. It renders a full-quality master itself; DaVinci Resolve Studio
  or Adobe Premiere Pro only adds an editable timeline.
- Is it only for professionals? No — built by professionals, designed for anyone making content.
- Is it free? Yes, completely: Apache 2.0, every feature, unlimited shoots, personal and client work.
- Can I modify or redistribute it? Yes. Keep the NOTICE file crediting FirstTake by Sklarstad LLC,
  keep the copyright lines, and mark changed files. Improvements are welcome as pull requests.
- Does it keep improving? Yes; every update is free on GitHub, and feature requests (GitHub issues or
  support@sklarstad.com) shape what gets built next.
